cross_ride.title: Under the hangers
cross_ride.what: from a standstill to the 6th support at a steady 10 m/s, dipping under the hanger at every support
cross_ride.note: Riding into a support her tips would meet the hanger, so at each one she lets go a tenth of a second or so before it, falls a few centimetres with her tips under the clamp, and reaches back for the wire once past it.

cross_fast.title: Fastest, every section
cross_fast.what: the least time from a standstill to the 6th support, full thrust on the wire, dipping under every hanger
cross_fast.note: Every moment off the wire is a moment without thrust: seven dips keep her off it for 1.2 s in all. The shortest lead that works wins (a tenth of a second; less and the tips have not dropped clear of the clamp), with poles held at 2.1 m so the reach has room to find the wire again. Hopping over the spans was not searched: each would cost a brake and a release.

cross_easy.title: Least effort
cross_easy.what: the least energy from a standstill to the 6th support within a minute, dipping under every hanger: coil work plus the work of pulling the poles in
cross_easy.note: Held speeds of 5 to 12 m/s were tried; the cheapest was 6 m/s (2.3 kJ, 29 s). Each dip costs a little: after the catch her poles are longer and she pulls them back in under load before the next support. Faster costs more in drag and in the push to get up to speed.

over_ride.title: Over the spans
over_ride.what: from a standstill to the 6th support, over the top of every cross-span, catching the wire in every section
over_ride.note: Nothing of her may pass under a hanger, so at every support she hops over the cross-span: a hard brake that swings her body forward and up, her poles pulled in through the bottom of the swing, and a release at the moment a look-ahead says all of her will clear the span and land on the wire more than a pole length past it. A twin of the game tries the launch out on the approach and starts it at the first moment it works.

over_fast.title: Over the spans, fastest
over_fast.what: the least time from a standstill to the 6th support, over the top of every cross-span, full thrust on the wire between hops
over_fast.note: Nothing of her may pass under a hanger, so at every support she hops over the cross-span: a hard brake that swings her body forward and up, her poles pulled in through the bottom of the swing, and a release at the moment a look-ahead says all of her will clear the span and land on the wire more than a pole length past it. A twin of the game tries the launch out on the approach and starts it at the first moment it works. Every hop starts with a brake to almost nothing, so full thrust between them buys little.

over_easy.title: Over the spans, least effort
over_easy.what: the least energy from a standstill to the 6th support within a minute, over the top of every cross-span: coil work plus the work of pulling the poles in
over_easy.note: Nothing of her may pass under a hanger, so at every support she hops over the cross-span: a hard brake that swings her body forward and up, her poles pulled in through the bottom of the swing, and a release at the moment a look-ahead says all of her will clear the span and land on the wire more than a pole length past it. A twin of the game tries the launch out on the approach and starts it at the first moment it works. Approach speeds of 6 to 15 m/s were tried; below 12 m/s she never got over every span, and 12 costs less than 15, so this is the same run as Over the spans. Most of the effort is the pull on her poles through the bottom of each launch.

fly_wing.title: Most on the wing
fly_wing.what: from a standstill to the 6th support flying as much of the way as she can with the wing spread, no cross-span met
fly_wing.note: The wing goes on only above the wires and comes off before she drops back through them; she lets go at the moment the look-ahead says the flight reaches farthest.

fly_most.title: Most in the air
fly_most.what: from a standstill to the 6th support with her body in the air as much of the way as it can be, by any means: flights with the wing, and the lifted gait between them
fly_most.note: In the air counts her time off the wire and her time riding it lifted, her weight on the wing. Riding lifted between supports was searched too (the pump entry into the lifted gait); it held for at most 7 % of the way and every such run ended on a cross-span, so the best is all flights.
